description: GEO-TREES site name. This should match the site name used elsewhere, e.g. `site_id` in the stem measurement table.

Acquisition ID. The tree inventory data collection event, to separate different GEO-TREES data collection campaigns. Commonly the mid-date of stem measurements within the site for this acquisition (census).
Plot name, unique within the site

Were plot dimensions established according to a planar projection? (TRUE/FALSE) I.e. was the distance between plot corners measured as a straight line as if looking down from above (TRUE), or following the ground surface (FALSE).
Length of plot (m)
Width of plot (m)
Additional notes on plot survey methods. E.g. methods to geo-locate plot corners, subplot layout.
Minimum diameter threshold (cm). I.e. the stem diameter above which stems are considered for measurement.
Default 'point of measurement' (POM) for diameter measurements (m). I.e. the height along the length of the stem where the stem diameter is measured.
For multi-stemmed trees, were measurements recorded for each stem? (TRUE/FALSE) I.e. were measurements recorded for every stem (TRUE), or only for one stem per tree (e.g. the largest stem) (FALSE)?
For multi-stemmed trees, are stems grouped into trees? (TRUE/FALSE) I.e. is it possible to identify to which tree each stem is attached?
Are dead stems measured? (TRUE/FALSE)
Are fallen stems measured? (TRUE/FALSE) Fallen is defined as the stem being on the ground and not supporting its own weight.
Are lianas measured? (TRUE/FALSE) If lianas are not present, enter "NA"
Are palms measured? (TRUE/FALSE) If palms are not present, enter "NA"
Are woody bamboos measured? (TRUE/FALSE) If woody bamboos are not present, enter "NA"
Describe the method used to geo-locate plot corners.
Describe the method used to map stems within the plot.
Link to protocol document used to measure these plots.  In order of preference: (1) DOI of published protocol, (2) reference of published protocol, (3) other URL, (4) link to local file.

Additional notes on measurements in the plot. Are other tree-like plants measured, e.g. cacti, banana plants, tree-ferns? Stem measurement and mapping methods. Clarification on TRUE/FALSE responses to previous questions.
Describe the anthropogenic status of the plot. E.g. old-growth, logged, secondary, plantation.
Describe the vegetation type of the plot. E.g. tropical evergreen broadleaf forest, tropical deciduous broadleaf, swamp forest, open savanna.
Describe any current or historic human land use in the plot. E.g. resource extraction, grazing, planting. Note any changes in land use and approximate dates.
Describe any current or historic experimental or management treatments which affect the plot. E.g. logging, prescribed fire, thinning, fertilizer application.
If fires affect this plot, describe the fire regime. E.g. number of years between fires, date of last fire, causes of fires, effects of fire on vegetation.
If cyclones affect this plot, describe the cyclone regime. E.g. number of years between cyclones, date of last cyclone, effects of cyclones on vegetation.
If this plot ever floods, describe the flooding. E.g. which plots are affected, frequency of flooding, date of last flood event.

If this plot ever experiences landslides, earthquakes or other earth movements, describe these phenomena. E.g. which plots are affected, date of last major earth movement event, effects of earth movements on the vegetation.
If herbivores affect the vegetation in this plot, describe the herbivory regime. E.g. species present, population size, effect on tree growth and mortality.
Describe any other disturbances which affect vegetation in this plot. E.g. pathogens, heat, frost, invasive species, windthrow.
